newsitem.title: USA: Accused N.C. killer called "monster" by attorneys.
newsitem.headline: Accused N.C. killer called "monster" by attorneys.

text.p: Defence attorneys for accused serial killer Henry Louis Wallace told jurors Wednesday they were going to "look inside the monster's mind" during what was expected to be his months-long trial for slaying nine young black women.

Wallace, 31, was arrested in March 1994 at the end of what police said was an 11-killing homicide spree that started in 1990 with a former South Carolina girlfriend and ended in March 1994 with the death of a former co-worker.
Wallace has been charged with nine of the 11 slayings and, if convicted, could face the death penalty in each case.

Testimony began Wednesday with opening arguments by Assistant District Attorney Marsha Goodenow who told the seven-woman, five-man jury they would hear Wallace convict himself in his own words during a 10-hour taped interview with police after his arrest.
In the tape, according to Goodenow, Wallace meticulously described how he strangled, stabbed, even burned one woman during the two-year string of homicides.
Each victim had five things in common, according to Goodenow. Each was an attractive black woman who was young, knew Wallace and died by his hand, she said.
Defence attorney Isabel Day said she does not deny that Wallace committed the murders, but said, "Henry Wallace is not in his right mind."

"This is terrible. Truly terrible," she said, looking out into an audience that included several family members of the victims. "There aren't any words to describe the absolute horror of these killings."
But she contended that the slayings did not fit the criteria for first-degree murder.

Day said she would call some of the nation's leading experts on serial murder and told the jury, "You may not like Henry Wallace ... (But) that isn't enough to find him guilty of a higher degree of murder than he is guilty of."
